newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent seen in $21-$25 band in Q1 - chartists.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent seen in $21-$25 band in Q1 - chartists.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures, which jumped to post-Gulf War highs in October, will likely vacillate between $21 and $25 a barrel in the first quarter of 1997, technical analysts said on Tuesday.

Brent failed to retest the six-year high of $25.06 during its rally last week and some momentum indicators showed divergence to the price action, underlining that the scorching rally of nearly 25 percent since summer has run out of steam.
"It looks as if we had a false break to new highs over the course of the last week," said Nicholas Wilson, technical analyst at MeesPierson. "It lacked conviction."
The front-month crude contract, which fell 15 cents at midday on Tuesday to $23.95, may bubble above its high from last week at $24.65, but not break $25, he said.
A double bottom at $22.49 from late November will be the first layer of long-term support, Wilson said, followed by previous lows near $21.80.
"It looks to me like the momentum of the whole up move has come close to a stop," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden in London.
"I expect it to consolidate and trade in a range from $21 to $24," he said.
The 20- and 40-week moving averages still supported the market, coming in at $22.67 and $20.86, respectively, and should prevent any vicious selloff, Haylor said.
Deeper support for spot Brent crude was placed at a downside gap from $21.45 to $21, which was registered in early September and has yet to be penetrated, chartists said.

A cautionary sign occurred when the Jan contract registered a new contract high last week of $24.65 but the Relative Strengh Index markers failed to reach their previous peaks, a bearish divergence, Wilson said.
"A number of trends broke during the course of the correction but the market continued to be well supported," he said. "There's still underlying strength in the market."
The current spot month Jan expires next Monday. Feb Brent was trading 14 cents lower at $23.32.
